sarah-sec: Heads up — ClearPath (private deployment) reported suspicious KMS decrypt activity tied to a service account they don't recognize. customer asking if keys were accessed externally. logs attached below.
priya-support: Thanks Sarah. Customer pressed us at 09:12 PDT. They've paused app traffic on their side and want immediate confirmation whether keys were used by us or a compromised svcacct.
priya-support: @matt-infra @josh-eng can infra confirm any admin console logins for their tenant or unusual node restarts?
matt-infra: Pulling tenant audit + node events now. I see several decrypt calls from a single svcacct: `svc-clearpath-runner@clearpath-tenant` between 02:03–02:07 UTC. IPs look to be internal VPC ranges but there's one outlier: 52.9.120.45. grabbing full flow.
incidents-bot: alert: tenant-decrypt-rate-spike detected for tenant clearpath-tenant at 2026-11-01T02:04:12Z (anomaly score 8.4)
josh-eng: Can you paste the KMS audit lines? Need to know which principal performed the decrypt and if it used a short-lived token or service account key.
matt-infra: Log snippet: ```[2026-11-01T02:04:12Z] tenant=clearpath-tenant principal=svc-clearpath-runner request=Decrypt key=kms-prod-01 result=OK src_ip=10.3.45.21 forwarded_for=52.9.120.45 token_type=access_token```
priya-support: The customer says they didn't rotate keys and did not create that svcacct recently. They want this contained ASAP.
alex-oncall: Proposed containment: 1) rotate tenant master key (or rotate SA permissions) 2) block source IP 52.9.120.45 at edge 3) snapshot tenant VM and export audit logs to S3 for forensics. Approve?
sarah-sec: Agree with containment but avoid rotating master key without hours-of-downtime warning to customer. Prefer to revoke the service account token(s) and add a temporary IAM deny for that svcacct, then rotate if we confirm compromise. Also we should request a signed attestation from ClearPath that they quarantined their app.
nina-platform: I can push a temporary deny policy to the tenant RBAC binding: `deny: principals: [svc-clearpath-runner@clearpath-tenant] actions: [kms:Decrypt] expires: 1h` — will that be acceptable for containment?
osh: note typo present (we should not include internal notes)
priya-support: Customer agreed to short outage for containment. Please execute deny.
matt-infra: Deny policy applied to tenant at 02:18 UTC. I also placed a network block for 52.9.120.45 at the VPC egress 02:19 UTC.
josh-eng: Running quick grep for other decrypts across tenants for that svcacct pattern. No other tenants show activity. Looks scoped to clearpath-tenant.
sarah-sec: Good. Next steps: 1) Full KMS access log export (all Decrypts for last 30 days) 2) Snapshot VM + process list at time of suspicious calls 3) Collect kube/instance metadata and deployed container images 4) Communicate back to ClearPath with what we found and ask for their endpoint logs for 02:00–02:10 UTC.
priya-support: Noted. @matt-infra can you export logs & snapshot and share a secure link to customer? Also include a minimal timeline for the customer.
matt-infra: Export started to secure-bucket (s3://redwood-forensics/clearpath/1839001234/) — ETA 18 minutes. Snapshot taken and stored.
sarah-sec: I'll open a formal incident ticket and run a quick vuln triage on the runner image for known CVEs. If we see an exploitation path we'll escalate to incident response.
josh-eng: One more ask: check KMS key-policy for any cross-tenant principals or overly-permissive roles. I remember we flagged this key in last month's config review as "expiring cert for role-binding" — verify there's no stray binding.
nina-platform: Key policy lookup done: no cross-tenant bindings. Binding shows `role: tenant-runner` granted to `svc-clearpath-runner@clearpath-tenant` and `infra-ops@redwood` — infra ops is expected. No wildcard principals.
sarah-sec: Good. If the customer confirms they didn't spin up the runner, next action is to rotate guest API keys used by their deployment and run a credential sweep.
priya-support: Customer appreciates quick containment. They asked for an interim explanation they can show their security team. Drafting now.
sarah-sec: Draft message ready, will share for review in #incidents after I attach export manifest.
incidents-bot: incident created: INC-20261101-042 (severity P2) assigned: sarah-sec, matt-infra, josh-eng
priya-support: Thanks team. I'll keep the customer in the loop and escalate to account exec if they get external counsel involved.
matt-infra: Export complete. link: [s3://redwood-forensics/clearpath/1839001234/manifest.json]
sarah-sec: Final note — follow-up: 24h log retention extension for this tenant, schedule a post-incident review, and verify automated alerting threshold that triggered. We'll reconvene in incident ticket.
